A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 25 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v4, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: V3 reports original membership-inference experiments on DDIM and Stable Diffusion, including benchmark results, ablations, normality tests, and defense evaluations.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds results for alternative filters, DiT, and threshold-selection strategies.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 retains the proposed Fourier-transform, frequency-mask, inverse-transform, and membership-scoring procedure. The default filter remains unchanged. Gaussian and Butterworth filters are tested as comparative alternatives, and the DiT experiment applies the existing attack.

E1.justification: V4 adds Mini-ImageNet data for DiT training and membership-inference evaluation in Appendix D.11. This extends image-dataset coverage while retaining the original datasets and membership-inference task.

E2.justification: V4 Table 20 adds Gaussian and Butterworth filtering as explicit comparison strategies alongside the default hard-cutoff filter. The attack comparator set remains Naive, SecMI, PIA, and CLID; CLID already appeared in v3 Appendix D.5.

E3.justification: V4 introduces threshold-selection/testing splits of 20%/80% by images or classes, a DiT evaluation with 1,400 training epochs and 256×256 images, and the overlap coefficient as a descriptive metric. These supplement the retained main protocols; the new shadow-model explanation does not establish a change to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices D.10 and D.12 add tests of filter-choice robustness and sensitivity to threshold-selection data. Section 5.3 quantitatively supplements the existing distribution visualization with overlap coefficients. Earlier hyperparameter, missing-caption, weak-overfitting, and defense analyses remain.

E5.justification: The Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests, significance level, and p-values are retained from v3 Table 8 in v4 Table 9. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals for attack performance. The new overlap coefficient measures separability rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: V4 adds filter, DiT, and threshold-split results in Tables 20–22 and overlap coefficients in Figure 2. Main benchmark scores remain unchanged. CLID's AUC and TPR values are retained, but its ASR entries are omitted. New Table 20 reports Gaussian/Butterworth average AUC gains of 9.16/9.17, whereas its displayed rows imply approximately 8.95/8.97.

T1.justification: Appendix C corrects Eq. C.11's left-side high-frequency variance term from the hold-out variance to the member variance. V4 also explicitly states component independence as an assumption before Eq. C.14. The proposition and remaining derivation largely retain their substance despite extensive notation substitutions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a unified attack paradigm, identification and theoretical analysis of high-frequency deficiency, and efficient filtering to improve attacks across datasets and models. Added evaluations support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly identifies the Gaussian approximation as a theoretical limitation and proposes distribution-free analysis as future work. It explains CLID's modest gains through near-ceiling performance and interprets the new filter comparisons as evidence of robustness. The pretraining limitation was already present in v3.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-repository URL, threshold-acquisition explanations, and DiT training details. Section 5.4 corrects the swapped filter-parameter values to match the existing setup and table, although the appendix retains the reversal. Section 5.1's shadow-model description and Appendix D.12's full-dataset threshold reuse are not clearly reconciled.

R1.justification: V4 adds discussion of autoregressive-model privacy attacks and Carlini et al.'s diffusion-model attack using LiRA, including applicability and computational-cost distinctions. It also adds references supporting the overlap coefficient and ImageNet evaluation. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing and reorganization are localized: CLID generality moves from Appendix D.5 to Section 5.6, limitations and impact statements move into the main text, and wording, notation, affiliations, and publication information are revised. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V4 merges v3's two CLID tables into one main-text table with fewer metric columns, adds Tables 20–22, and annotates Figure 2 with overlap values. Existing displays are relocated or resized, while the overall visual format and most figure content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The separate threshold-selection tests, filter comparisons, and DiT evaluation strengthen validation of the retained method. The explicit Gaussian limitation and corrected proof term also improve qualification and accuracy. These bounded gains outweigh the loss of CLID ASR reporting, although inconsistent averages in new Table 20 and unreconciled threshold descriptions limit the improvement.
